idiom: hit the nail on the head
meaning: to describe or identify exactly the right point or problem
example: You hit the nail on the head when you said the ad was too long.
origin: Comes from carpentry, where a hammer strikes the head of a nail to drive it in exactly

wrong_meanings.meaning: to hammer something into a wall
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the literal image, not the idiomatic meaning; the idiom is about being accurate, not about construction

wrong_meanings.meaning: to make the same mistake again and again
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom praises being exactly right, so it does not describe repeated errors

wrong_meanings.meaning: to finish a project very quickly
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom refers to accuracy of judgment or description, not to speed of work

explanation: 'Hit the nail on the head' means that someone has described or identified the exact cause or point of something. It is used to praise an accurate comment.
